cleanup.note: each arm is measured on its own graph and NO graph is dropped. `reset()` runs once per population and acts on the graph the last arm left current, so one graph per population is emptied and the rest are left POPULATED. On a lane container `test_lane.py down` disposes of them, which is the intended path; a shared server accumulates one full set per run.

coverage_map.why_no_bytes_per_node: F is dimensionless, so the coverage<->MB map is independent of the per-node byte figure (§17.4.2: the declared 1,024 B matches no measured regime; measured 1,672 B/resident node). The byte dispute moves NODE COUNTS, not this curve.

per_tenant_size.why: pp/MB is S-dependent by construction (W = F x S), so this answers 'for a tenant this size, by which MB has the window flattened' — never a property of the curve

scale_free.why: a DOUBLING of the window is dimensionless, so this is the knee in the SHAPE of the curve, independent of tenant size — quote this one about the shape

floor.note: no window can buy a miss rate below this on this label, AT THIS POPULATION SIZE
floor.population_scale_caveat: measured on 1000 nodes at depth 50. At production scale (tens of thousands of nodes) MORE documents compete for the same 50 ranks, so this is a LOWER bound on the production ceiling, not an estimate of it. Read the DIRECTION and the ORDER of magnitude, never the decimal.
floor.source: the complete-graph arm's miss (nothing is demoted, so it is the leg's own unreachability)

largest_tenant_mb.why: inverts mb_for_miss: the LARGEST tenant graph a tier's window still keeps at or below a miss bar. This is the '#13989 not nudged in week two' number — a tenant SIZE, not a rate. None = the bar is unreachable at any window.

sensitivity.why: the mass is a RECURRENCE proxy, not an observed read ledger; this re-runs the curve over a Zipf family bracketing the fitted concentration so the flattening point is a RANGE

labels_measured.object: :Object — the entity dictionary; the label the residency booster exists for
labels_measured.point: :Point — the claim population; the label the window demotes
labels_measured.\u26d4not_measured: :Subject shares :Object's harvest class and leg and is not separately populated; :Source and :Event are anchored/key reads and a window does not move them the same way. No aggregate across labels is published.

uniform_query_control.why: uniform query weighting makes fault_in_rate == 1 - F exactly; the curve is a straight line and nothing flattens. M2 drew its queries uniformly at random, so this — not the window — is what its policy comparison measured.

windows.note: solo 77 / pro 102 / team 615 are the SHIPPED values; this artifact measures what they buy and never changes them
